data.hypothesis: The supplied T1 candidates are all valid and have repeated aggregate means of 0.01140523 s (4x256x16), 0.01587444 s (8x128x32), and 0.02015676 s (8x64x32), but no per-size timings are available to attribute a result specifically to n=1024. This contrasting 4x128x16 scheme assigns independent row/column output tiles under static OpenMP scheduling, potentially improving cache residency and work distribution at large sizes; the smaller tiles and extra tile-loop work may instead hurt. It retains serial execution below n=256 and contiguous i-k-j output-column updates.

memory_lessons.claim: Among the three supplied valid T1 trials, the reported aggregate mean was lowest for 4x256x16 (0.01140523 s), followed by 8x128x32 (0.01587444 s) and 8x64x32 (0.02015676 s). Each had repeated timings, but no per-size breakdown is shown.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the 4x128x16 collapsed output-tile ownership variant with repeated native timings and compare n=1024 specifically, without inferring a result from aggregate means alone.

data.notes: This proposal replaces the current fixed-size dispatch with generic positive-n handling, zeroes the complete output on each call, and keeps inputs read-only. The supplied history contains three valid T1 trials and no recorded failed attempt; no failure is inferred. No new timings or correctness results are claimed. Per-size timing is unavailable in the supplied observations, so the n=1024 effect remains to be measured.
transformations: Replace fixed-size dispatch with generic handling for every positive n and zero the complete output before accumulation.
Use unpacked 4x128x16 row/column/K tiles with ascending K blocks and an i-k-j update whose innermost output-column loop is contiguous.
Assign disjoint row/column output tiles with static collapsed OpenMP scheduling for n >= 256; run serially below that threshold or when only one worker is requested.
Clamp the requested worker count to the range 1..8; do not pack matrices or use explicit intrinsics.
